newsitem.title: FINLAND: EMU DOOMED IF DELAYED BEYOND 99 - FINNISH PROFESSOR.
newsitem.headline: EMU DOOMED IF DELAYED BEYOND 99 - FINNISH PROFESSOR.

text.p: Postponing economic and monetary union (EMU) beyound the planned 1999 start would mean that the project would fail, a Finnish professor said on Wednesday.

Speaking at an EMU seminar arranged by training institute IIR Finland, Turku University politics professor Esko Antola said politicians' commitment to EMU was so strong that a failure would mean an end to European integration as it is known now.

"Leaders at the summit on May 1 (1998) can of course decide anything they want in principle, but if you consider the amount of commitment, (deciding on a delay) would likely make EMU not happen," Antola said.
"If EMU were to fail, then this integration model would fall, and likely in a couple of years, a new EMU would be built by only those who really want it, aiming directly at a federal state," he said.
Antola also said he could not imagine a successful EMU without federal fiscal policy in the single currency area.
